entries.problem: A buzzer sounds after the refrigerator door has been open for more than 3 minutes
entries.possibleCause: The refrigerator door has remained open for more than 3 minutes.
entries.safeUserCheck: Close the refrigerator door. The alarm can also be silenced by pressing any button, but if the door remains open the alarm will sound again after 3 minutes.
entries.claimTrigger: No service claim is required when the alarm is caused by the refrigerator door being left open.
entries.sourceSection: PDF pp. 45-46, CONTROLS - Appliance controls

entries.problem: The fridge-freezer does not work
entries.possibleCause: The electric circuit may be disrupted, the plug may not be correctly inserted, the appliance power cable may be damaged, the socket may have no power, or the appliance may not be switched on.
entries.safeUserCheck: Check that the plug is correctly inserted. Check whether the power cable is visibly damaged. Check whether the socket has power using another normal appliance. Check that the appliance is switched on.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim if the appliance still does not work after the safe power and control checks. Stop using the appliance if the power cable is damaged.
evidenceToRequest: photo or video showing that the appliance does not operate
description of the plug and socket checks
description of whether the power cable is visibly damaged
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 54, TROUBLE-SHOOTING

entries.problem: The lighting inside the appliance does not work
entries.possibleCause: For appliances with bulb lighting, the bulb may be loose or fused. A general appliance power problem can also prevent the light from working.
entries.safeUserCheck: First perform the safe checks listed for an appliance that does not work. If the appliance uses a replaceable bulb, check the user-replaceable bulb as described in the manual.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim if the appliance has power but the interior lighting still does not work after the supported user check.
evidenceToRequest: photo or video showing the lighting problem
description of whether the appliance otherwise operates normally
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 54, TROUBLE-SHOOTING

entries.problem: The appliance operates continuously
entries.possibleCause: The temperature setting may be incorrect, or one of the conditions listed for insufficient cooling may be causing prolonged operation.
entries.safeUserCheck: Adjust the temperature setting as described in the manual. Also check the safe external causes listed for incorrect temperature, including door opening, food placement, ventilation, heat sources, and ambient temperature.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim if the appliance continues to operate continuously after the supported external checks and correct settings.
evidenceToRequest: description of how often the doors are opened
description of ventilation and installation conditions
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 54, TROUBLE-SHOOTING

entries.problem: Water collects in the lower part of the refrigerator
entries.possibleCause: The condensate discharge opening may be clogged, or internal air circulation may be obstructed because food or containers touch the rear wall.
entries.safeUserCheck: If the appliance has a condensate discharge opening, carefully clean it using the cleaning plug as described in the manual. Arrange food and containers so they do not touch the rear wall.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim if water continues to collect after the discharge opening and food placement have been checked.
evidenceToRequest: photo of the rear wall and food placement
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 54, TROUBLE-SHOOTING

entries.problem: The refrigerator condensate discharge opening requires cleaning
entries.possibleCause: Contaminants carried with condensate during defrosting can clog the discharge opening.
entries.safeUserCheck: Disconnect the appliance from the mains before cleaning. Carefully unclog the discharge opening using the cleaning plug described in the manual.
entries.claimTrigger: No service claim is required for normal accessible drain cleaning. Create a claim if drainage remains blocked or water continues to collect.
evidenceToRequest: photo of the drain area if the problem continues
description of whether drainage improved after cleaning
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 52, DEFROSTING, WASHING AND MAINTENANCE - Defrosting the fridge

entries.problem: The appliance makes unusual noise
entries.possibleCause: The appliance may not be level or may be touching furniture or other objects.
entries.safeUserCheck: Check that the appliance is level and stable. Make sure it has proper clearance and is not touching adjacent furniture or other objects.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim if unusual noise continues after the appliance is correctly levelled and separated from surrounding objects.
evidenceToRequest: video or audio of the unusual noise
description of levelling and clearance checks
entries.sourceSection: PDF pp. 54-55, TROUBLE-SHOOTING

entries.problem: Cracking, compressor, thermostat, or refrigerant-flow sounds are heard during operation
entries.possibleCause: The manual states that these sounds can occur during normal operation because of the thermostat, compressor switching, refrigerant flow, and thermal expansion and contraction of components.
entries.safeUserCheck: No corrective action is required if the sound matches normal operating sounds described in the manual.
entries.claimTrigger: Do not create a service claim for normal operating sounds alone. Create a claim if the noise is clearly abnormal and remains after the external installation checks.
entries.sourceSection: PDF pp. 38 and 55, GUIDELINES CONCERNING THE SAFETY OF USE / TROUBLE-SHOOTING

entries.problem: Temperature inside the fridge-freezer is not low enough or is too high
entries.possibleCause: Possible causes listed by the manual include an incorrect temperature setting, ambient temperature outside the appliance climate range, direct sunlight or nearby heat sources, a large quantity of warm food, obstructed internal or rear air circulation, frequent or prolonged door opening, a door that does not close completely, the compressor switching on too rarely, or an incorrectly inserted door gasket.
entries.safeUserCheck: Check the temperature setting and ambient conditions. Make sure the appliance is away from direct sunlight and heat sources, allow up to 72 hours after loading a large amount of warm food, keep food away from the rear wall, keep at least 30 mm clearance behind the appliance, reduce unnecessary door opening, check that food does not prevent the door from closing, and check that the accessible door gasket is correctly seated.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim if the temperature remains incorrect after the supported external checks and sufficient cooling time.
evidenceToRequest: photo showing food placement and door closure
description of ambient and installation conditions
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 55, TROUBLE-SHOOTING

entries.problem: The refrigerator or freezer door does not close completely
entries.possibleCause: Food or containers may interfere with closing, or the door gasket may be incorrectly inserted.
entries.safeUserCheck: Arrange food and containers so they do not interfere with the door. Check that the accessible door gasket is correctly seated.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim if the door still does not close completely after food placement and the door gasket have been checked.
evidenceToRequest: photo or video showing the door not closing
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 55, TROUBLE-SHOOTING

entries.problem: The door gasket is damaged
entries.possibleCause: The manual does not specify the cause of gasket damage. It states that a damaged seal must be replaced because otherwise the door will not shut properly.
entries.safeUserCheck: Keep the door gasket clean and visually check whether it is damaged or incorrectly seated. Do not dismantle the appliance.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim if the door gasket is damaged and requires replacement.
evidenceToRequest: photo of the damaged door gasket
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 50, USING THE REFRIGERATOR EFFICIENTLY - Practical everyday tips

entries.problem: The freezer door is difficult to reopen immediately after it has been closed
entries.possibleCause: Negative pressure can temporarily form inside the freezer after the door is closed.
entries.safeUserCheck: Wait 1 to 2 minutes for the pressure to equalise, then try opening the freezer door again. Do not force the door.
entries.claimTrigger: No service claim is required if the door opens normally after waiting for the pressure to equalise.
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 49, OPERATION AND FUNCTIONS - Freezing food

entries.problem: Condensation appears above the vegetable containers
entries.possibleCause: Vegetables containing significant quantities of water can cause condensation to form above the vegetable containers.
entries.safeUserCheck: No corrective action is required for this condensation alone. Dry vegetables well before storing them, as recommended by the manual.
entries.claimTrigger: Do not create a service claim for this normal condensation alone.
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 48, OPERATION AND FUNCTIONS - Storage of food in the fridge-freezer

entries.problem: Frost forms on the rear wall of the refrigerator compartment
entries.possibleCause: The appliance operates in cooling and defrosting cycles. Frost can form on the rear wall and is removed automatically. In automatic-defrost models, frost can also appear when large quantities of fresh food are stored.
entries.safeUserCheck: No corrective action is required when frost appears and disappears as part of the normal defrosting cycle.
entries.claimTrigger: Do not create a service claim for normal rear-wall frost that clears during automatic defrosting. Create a claim if abnormal ice accumulation persists and normal operation is affected.
evidenceToRequest: photo of persistent abnormal frost if it does not clear
description of how long the frost remains
entries.sourceSection: PDF pp. 52-53, DEFROSTING, WASHING AND MAINTENANCE - Defrosting the fridge / Automatic fridge defrosting

entries.problem: Small temperature changes occur inside the appliance
entries.possibleCause: The manual states that slight temperature changes are normal, for example after storing large quantities of fresh food or leaving the door open for a longer period.
entries.safeUserCheck: Allow the appliance to return to the selected temperature. Avoid leaving the door open longer than necessary.
entries.claimTrigger: Do not create a service claim for slight temporary temperature fluctuations that return to the selected setting.
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 47, CONTROLS - Additional information on the temperature

entries.problem: Fast Cool switches off automatically
entries.possibleCause: The Fast Cool function is designed to switch off automatically after its programmed operating period or after the relevant temperature condition is reached, depending on the control version.
entries.safeUserCheck: No corrective action is required when Fast Cool switches off automatically as described in the manual.
entries.claimTrigger: Do not create a service claim for automatic Fast Cool deactivation alone.
entries.sourceSection: PDF pp. 45-46, CONTROLS - Appliance controls

entries.problem: The appliance power cable is damaged
entries.possibleCause: The manual does not provide a customer-repairable cause. A damaged supply cord must be replaced by the manufacturer, service agent, or similarly qualified person to avoid a hazard.
entries.safeUserCheck: Stop using the appliance. Disconnect it from the mains only if this can be done safely. Do not repair or replace the power cable yourself.
entries.claimTrigger: Create an urgent service claim for a damaged power cable or exposed electrical parts.
evidenceToRequest: photo of the damaged cable if safe to take
description of when the damage was noticed
entries.sourceSection: PDF pp. 38-40, GUIDELINES CONCERNING THE SAFETY OF USE

entries.problem: The refrigerant circuit or refrigerant pipe is damaged
entries.possibleCause: The cooling system or refrigerant pipe has been punctured, broken, or otherwise damaged. The manual states that the refrigerant is flammable.
entries.safeUserCheck: Stop using the appliance. Do not touch, bend, puncture, or attempt to repair the refrigerant circuit. Ventilate the room for several minutes. Keep ignition sources away and contact service.
entries.claimTrigger: Create an urgent service claim for any confirmed or suspected refrigerant-circuit damage.
evidenceToRequest: photo of visible damage if safe to take
description of how the damage occurred
description of any unusual sound, smell, or loss of cooling
entries.sourceSection: PDF pp. 38-40 and 42, GUIDELINES CONCERNING THE SAFETY OF USE / INSTALLATION AND OPERATING CONDITIONS OF THE APPLIANCE

entries.problem: Refrigerant has come into contact with the eyes
entries.possibleCause: Refrigerant has escaped from a damaged cooling system and contacted the eyes.
entries.safeUserCheck: Rinse the eyes with clean water and seek medical assistance immediately. Do not attempt to repair the cooling system.
entries.claimTrigger: Stop using the appliance and create an urgent service claim because refrigerant leakage indicates damage to the cooling system.
evidenceToRequest: description of how the refrigerant release occurred
photo of visible appliance damage if safe to take
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 38, GUIDELINES CONCERNING THE SAFETY OF USE

entries.problem: The fridge-freezer was tilted by more than 40 degrees during transport, moving, or positioning
entries.possibleCause: The appliance was transported or positioned at an angle greater than the limit stated by the manual.
entries.safeUserCheck: Place the appliance correctly and wait at least 2 hours before switching it on.
entries.claimTrigger: No service claim is required if the appliance operates normally after being correctly positioned and left for at least 2 hours. Create a claim if it does not operate correctly afterward.
evidenceToRequest: description of how the appliance was transported
description of how long it stood upright before being switched on
matchTerms: when can I turn fridge on
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 38, GUIDELINES CONCERNING THE SAFETY OF USE

entries.problem: The fridge-freezer has a malfunction that requires repair
entries.possibleCause: The manual does not provide a customer-repairable cause for faults that remain after the documented troubleshooting checks.
entries.safeUserCheck: Do not repair or modify the appliance yourself. If the malfunction remains after the safe checks in the manual, contact service and have the appliance serial number ready.
entries.claimTrigger: Create a service claim when a malfunction remains after the supported safe user checks.
evidenceToRequest: photo or video showing the malfunction
entries.sourceSection: PDF p. 56, WARRANTY AND AFTER SALES SERVICE - Service
